correctness.rationale: Area-uniform sampling is normalized by (n-2)π. In a cusp width h_i the strip integral is 2 sinh(s)[1+log(h_i/(2sinh(s)))]; compact geodesic strips contribute L0 sinh(s)+O_P(s²). Therefore leading coefficient is 2n/((n-2)π) and the next numerator is L0+2∑log h_i+2n(1-log2). Horocyclic cancellation produces the Möbius-invariant chord product. For a quadrilateral Ptolemy gives ratio (x+y)^2/(xy)>=4, with equality at x=y. For a standard ideal triangle the (v,w) area integral yields the displayed exact CDF, support [0, asinh(1/√3)], density and 3√3/π quadratic endpoint tail. Independent symbolic differentiation and evaluation checked the CDF/density identity, F(rho)=1 and sharp quadratic tail coefficient; no uniform bound under cusp degeneration asserted.
residual_risks: The second-order compact/cusp seam estimate is for each fixed nondegenerate polygon only; degenerating shapes can change the error bounds.
